learning_outcomes.text: Are able to analyze and evaluate the stresses on machine parts and structures under static mechanical loads, and to dimension these components.
Are able to calculate stresses arising in components due to loads such as tension/compression, bending, torsion, or combined loading, and to evaluate them using strength hypotheses.

Are particularly able to confidently handle three-dimensional problems, can reliably distinguish and calculate straight and oblique bending, can calculate area moments and bending resistance moments of composite cross-sections, as well as torsional area moments and torsional resistance moments of thin-walled closed and open cross-sections, and of general cross-sections.
Can calculate deformations on beam-like components, also for statically indeterminate structures.
Understand Euler's buckling cases and can confidently solve related problems.
Understand the concept of the stress tensor and can perform coordinate transformations and calculate principal stresses.
Can evaluate multiaxial stress states using equivalent stresses.
Know the linear elastic constitutive law for plane stress states and three-dimensional problems and can confidently apply it.
Know the fundamental concepts of elastostatics and can competently express themselves, discuss, and professionally explain calculated results in the field of strength of materials.
Are able to confidently apply mathematical principles for calculations.
Possess abstract thinking skills and can solve tasks independently and in a structured way in a team.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to the fundamental concepts and relationships of strength of materials
Multiaxial stress states, transformation relationships, stress tensor, principal stresses, Mohr's circle
Linear elastic constitutive law, also for multiaxial stress states
Types of stress, such as tension-compression, bending, torsion, and the resulting stresses and deformations
Combined stress, calculation of stress tensor and deformations
Extensive practice examples for the confident application of what has been learned to engineering tasks according to the degree program
